1.准备阶段花费的食材准备太长，我们是三~四人游玩的，基本每次在接待结束后，就需要花费大量的时间来进行食材的补充，但是基本负责外围的两个哥们就无事可做只能等着或进来帮忙放东西 你要问我为什么他们不来帮忙，这个问题我会在后面的点提到。 2.菜品实际赚取的钱其实很少，收益未达到预期，我们联机的存档已经到达36天，但是金钱数额停留在五千已经很久了，每天购买食材实际上会花费大量的金币，很难积累，即使在36天这样的时间 我们也很难购买像冰箱这样的东西来帮助我们储存菜品，并且我们每天都会通过号角来召唤额外的客人，但金额数仍然是入不敷出。 3.储存位置太稀缺，希望官方能出更多的储存来帮助后厨减少食材储备压力，比如更大的架子或者更多的厨房面积。 后厨实际上是非常拥挤的，厨具会占用大量的地盘，但是又必须将每天所需要的 食材放在架子上来进行拿取，所以厨房会显得非常的拥挤。 4.目前税收对于我来讲还是算比较高的，房间和架子，以及我们未购买的餐盘（这个东西真的非常的贵！他高达70元！），所以希望官方能够对现有的税收，包括菜品价格进行调整。 争对上面的问题，我有以下建议： 1.在准备阶段提供额外的buff加持，让玩家能够进行更快的切菜和烧烤；如果觉得难做，可以提高玩家技能触发的概率和触发的时间，让玩家能在准备阶段进行更少的时间来准备，保证有更多的精力 在营业阶段，你会好奇为什么我们不购买官方为我们准备好的半成品，我会回答：他的价格不会让我去考虑购买他，因为就算我只购买最基础的材料自己去制作半成品，我也很难赚取更多的钱。 2.下调菜品价格，同时减少物品税收，调整物品过高税收的价格，这个其实是影响玩家赚钱的最直接原因，所以很重要。 3.提供更大的架子，让玩家可以多储存食材，包括更高的架子，比如4格架子，我在游戏里尝试过应该是能够到的，或者例如壁挂这种能让玩家将箱子放置在墙上储存，解放地上空间。 这些都是我和我的朋友们在游玩时候的真实体验，希望官方可以以此参考进行游戏优化，提供更好的游戏体验，我们全是从demo版本开始就支持鼠鼠餐厅的玩家，在发行也是进行了第一时间的购买。 所以对这游戏也有自己的心血和热爱在里面，能看见这游戏变得更好也是我们的心愿，后续如果在游玩体验上有新的意见我们也会即使反馈给官方。 1.The ingredient preparation in the preparation phase takes too long. We play with 3-4 people, and basically, after each reception, we need to spend a lot of time replenishing ingredients. However, the two guys responsible for the front-of-house usually have nothing to do but wait or come in to help put things away. You might ask why they don’t come to help – I’ll address this in a later point. 2.The actual profit from the dishes is very low, failing to meet expectations. Our online save file has reached Day 36, but the money has been stuck at 5,000 for a long time. Buying ingredients every day actually costs a lot of gold coins, making it hard to accumulate wealth. Even by Day 36,we still struggle to afford items like a refrigerator to help store dishes. We also use the horn to summon extracustomers every day, but we’re still spending more than we earn. 3.Storage space is extremely scarce. We hope the developers can add more storage options to reduce the pressure of ingredient storage in the kitchen, such as larger shelves or more kitchen space. The kitchen is actually very cramped – kitchen utensils take up a lot of room, but we have to place the daily needed ingredients on the shelves for easy access, which makes the kitchen even more crowded. 4.The current tax rate is quite high for us, including taxes on rooms, shelves, and even the unpurchased dinner plates (they are really expensive – up to 70 gold coins!). We hope the developers can adjust the existing taxrates, including dish prices. Suggestions for the above issues: 1.Provide additional buffs during the preparation phase to allow players to chop ingredients and grill faster. If that‘s too difficult to implement, increase the probability and duration of skill activations for players. This way, players can spend less time preparing and save more energy for the business phase. You might wonder why we don’t buy the pre-made semi-finished products provided by the developers. My answer is: their prices are too high to consider. Even if I only buy the most basic ingredients to make semi- finished products myself, it’s still hard to make more money. 2.Lower dish prices and reduce item taxes, especially adjusting the excessively high tax rates on items. This is actually the most direct factor affecting players’ ability to earn money, so it’s crucial. 3.Add larger storage shelves to allow players to store more ingredients – such as taller shelves (e.g., 4-slot shelves, which I’ve tried in the game and can reach) or wall-mounted storage options that let players place boxes on the wall, freeing up floor space. These are the real experiences of me and my friends while playing. We hope the developers can use these as references to optimize the game and provide a better gaming experience. All of us have supported "Shu Shu Restaurant" since the demo version and purchased it immediately upon its official release. We have invested a lot of passion and effort into this game, and it’s our wish to see it get better. We will continue to provide timely feedback to the developers if we have new suggestions during future gameplay.

Really liked the game until a MAGA hat started showing up on the Wheel of Fortune. Dev's attitude was really flippant, and it's a non-serious game. I don't understand why politics are included at all. Unfortunate, because the game itself is really fun, but I don't play games to deal with my everyday life. I did uninstall and refund. If you're not affected by the MAGA movement, and don't care about the cosmetic, it's a fun game for friends. If you don't support MAGA or are bothered by it being included in the game, I don't recommend buying it.

There is a MAGA hat cosmetic available in game. A hate symbol being used as a joke while thousands of people are actually suffering at the hands of the vermin who wear it. Its not cute, its not funny, it is in fact DISGUSTING. After it was brought up in a steam discussion board the devs deleted the initial post bringing attention to the hateful cosmetic. A second post was made reiterating consumer concerns and only then did the devs actually respond with a measly "We think its funny! Its not that serious :)" after which we were encouraged to refund the game. At the end of the day the hat is a hate symbol. You can claim it’s “just a silly cosmetic” but it’s literally a representation of a hateful movement lead by an evil man. By downplaying the severity of the item and its IRL impact you are silently aligning yourself with its original views, even more so after consumers have vocalized its negative impact on them. It’s not just “oh I don’t have to wear this cosmetic” we don’t even NEED it in the game. It adds nothing but strife and a reminder that there are actual disgusting humans in the world that rally behind that movement. There are NO OTHER political items making a mockery of certain movements which makes that argument null and void. Games are about escapism and this is a dose of a hateful reality that drives fear into lives. This game was so much fun but the way you’ve handled the commentary and conversation regarding the matter is disheartening. It’s truly a shame to have to refund an entertaining game over a MAGA hat knockoff. I hope your able to reflect on your player bases concerns more seriously in the future. Do better.

Overall wouldn't recommend due to a lack of fleshed-out content to justify a $20 USD game and MAGA-leaning devs. Genuinely thought this game must've been in early access because of the lack of content and wonky, not fully fleshed out mechanics. The skill tree is just repeated full of the same uncreative perks and doesn't fully lean into its potential, making it feel boring and stale after just a few hours of playing. The cooking mechanics are complex enough to be fun, but the setup requires at least one person hosting and one person cooking - the hosting player will consistently receive less XP comparatively and have just enough to do to not justify running the long trek to the kitchen. Something that would help with this is allowing the drink jugs to be placed in the dining rooms too, as a "bartender" kinda vibe, so the host player could at least fulfill drink requests this way. Additionally, not sure how to see reputation, or how that impacts the restaurant, but we've had to buy multiple of the "call extra customer" furniture items because otherwise we'd just be standing around waiting for more customers despite empty seats and positive reviews. The rate at which you earn the ability to buy new items is also a bit frustratingly slow, and are random, so it often feels like a way to make the game feel longer with less content. Also I do not believe "roguelike/"roguelite" is an accurate descriptor, so just fyi if that is important to you. Their content roadmap has no dates, with the free updates containing a disproportionate amount of cosmetic plans, and with the state of the game as it is, is not a great outlook for the future. As of writing this, I've played about 3 hours and have run into a few one-off bugs that were confusing and also led to my thinking it must be in early access, due to how common and basic the bugs were (like items completely disappearing after making them, for example). Devs also don't care that MAGA isn't just a joke for some folks. They have a MAGA hat you can randomly unlock, and the first time someone posted about how this upset them, they had their post deleted, and the second time the developers left a half-hearted "just don't use it, it's funny". This leaves a bad taste in my mouth and I wish I knew this before buying the game as I wouldn't have supported them knowing this. Makes sense that a game half-baked would be produced by folks with half-baked thoughts.

I love playing this game with my friends but it KILLS ME to see AI generated slop all over, especially as a graphic artist. Hopefully with the money they receive from buyers of this game, they'll actually pay artists to update their typography and rat icons shown throughout the game. When I look at Steam reviews of this game, I see a lot of people calling out the usage of AI and the developers deny all claims. But if you simply take a screenshot of the AI generated image/type and put it through an AI image detector, it always comes back as a 90%+ rating as "yes" it was AI generated. Again, I love playing this game with my friends but it kills me to support AI slop.

Fundamentally, I think the game is relatively fun and hectic, the same sort of fun you would get from those supermarket simulator style games. I believe the progression could be improved, it feels just a bit slow during the prep time and a bit too fast during serving hours. How are 3 rats supposed to handle two couriers and a VIP hitting nearly all at the same time? Completely insurmountable task for I believe was day 17 or so. The reason my review is negative is simple, I simply do not agree with AI generated assets being used in games, and I definitely don't like that there was no disclaimer for it on the store page. I've read the comments prior to writing this review, and I'm not the only one who's noticing; I've also noticed the dev says "there is no AI in our game" which is unfortunate because the dev either does not know it's AI and was lied to about it by an artist, or is outright lying themselves. The most prominent gen AI asset I've seen is the skill tree rat in the center. I believe the title text "RESTAURATS" was AI assisted, but those are the only two notable AI generated assets I've spotted. In my opinion, it's better to outright replace art that people are calling AI generated even if it's not AI generated, because it will keep getting negative reactions from people who are against it. (or at the very least, replace it with better looking AI assets!)

I would have never gotten this game if I had known there was AI in it. I unfortunately got it because they didn't add that section to their description, which I'm pretty sure goes against Steam's TOS. You could have gotten artists to help with making the logo and trailers, labels for the boxes, and other places that I may not have seen the AI slop generated at, but they chose not to. I am completely and utterly disgusted and disappointed. Regardless, from the bit I played before realizing this, it was pretty hectic, a lot needs to be improved about it (i.e.: not enough space in the kitchen, recipes take too long to make, the UI is all over the place and does not make sense, the goblin takes way too long to deliver things and they only deliver it one at a time, etc..). This made a game that was supposed to be about cooking not fun at all. I'd say I would come back to this if the above was improved, but since there's AI in it that wasn't even provided in the information about this game, I will never be coming back. EDIT: For anyone having doubts about this, I actually did play it. I played it on stream. I unpublished the VOD because I don't stand with AI at all, but I still have the recording to show it. It is true, the game itself probably does not have AI and it's probably just very janky. However, people in my chat told me to look at the ORIGINAL trailers during it. You can check it on IGN, they have the original trailers posted. Clothing wrinkles that do not make sense, a rat having five fingers on a hand instead of four, the pupils of the eyes literally bulging out...You can't tell me that's not AI. To the devs that are trying to tell me otherwise, record the ENTIRE Blender scene with the bare bones to prove me wrong. I saw your tweet, so you'd have no problem sharing that, right?

As it stands; I wouldn't recommend it. I thought the gameplay was neat, but kept checked the storepage at some point. No AI disclosure. After a bit of playtime, checked out some comments to confirm there's AI usage. Was going to continue playing with a friend, because another friend posted a thread on reddit where the developer (Alyssa) confirmed AI use, BUT that it would be replaced by real artists. Figured ok, when they go through with that, I'll buy the game. Went through some more steam reviews, to find the same developer seeming to claim 'There's no AI in the game', as well as links to spotify and the trailer, and the credits. Everything was done by artists (this was November). In game's discussions, there's been an update in their discord as of July 2025, stating there IS AI in the game, but it's meant as a placeholder due to being a small team. I don't really get if that just means they added the AI later, or something was miscommunicated in November or what happened, but it really killed my mood for the game entirely to have to run around for something that should be a disclaimer on the main store page. I don't know if there's a reason the AI wasn't admitted to in November, nor if there's a particular reason it isn't labelled on the base page. May revisit this once the placeholders are gone, but I really dislike how unclear it seems to be. Im not a fan of Generative AI, and I know a lot of people don't care, but at the very least I expect it to be said when it's used. Further edit: A month past, and still no proper AI disclosure as steam requires. Regardless of feeling on genAI in games, this game should not be an exception, and should disclose it properly instead of in a private place on their discord, or in a reply to a review from a while back. 0 reason not to disclose. If you don't want to risk losing sales, that's the risk you run including it.

Free weekend reviews don't count towards total, so: wouldn't have liked to have spent money on this. It's probably alright if you just want to fool around as funny rats and don't look too closely. Just don't expect it to be the next Overcooked, PlateUp, or any other cooking/automation game that you hold dear. Visual [list] [*] Good rats and general 3d art direction [*] Very mediocre 2d art, some of it visibly AI-generated. Just the general contrast between the game's 3d art and this sight when you level up: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3732199376 The skill tree specifically has it pretty bad as most icons don't read easily, especially when they're locked and darkened. [/list] Game design [list] [*] Too many things in this game are "pay/invest a point for a +2% boost" [*] Also has per-player levelling system with a MMO-esque skill tree, which too largely consists of "+3% to something" blocks. [*] You cannot (?) retrain the said skills [*] Most experience is granted for the kitchen work so some players will be visibly higher-level than others unless you swap places often [*] As you add more recipes, the preparation phase starts taking longer than the play phase. The recently introduced automation-raccoons help, but only to an extent. [*] "Tax" system (most appliances cost N gold per day, additional appliances have logarithmic cost increases) only further reinforces the "prepare as much as you can before the day starts" play style. [*] Recipe cards do very little at communicating what exactly it's going to take to cook that dish. [/list] UX: [list] [*] No FOV slider Which usually isn't much of an issue in a third-person game, but FOV is locked to vertical, so if you have a 16:10/3:2 display, the camera is zoomed and you can see less. [*] Customer voice lines are rather few, get old very quickly, and cannot be disabled separately. [*] Really could be showing the name of the item you are holding/about to pick up as many of these look similar enough to each other. [/list] Localization [list] [*] English localization is pretty bad, either machine-translated or hastily translated without context/communication. Without being able to check the exact wording now, "+n% customer patience" was translated in such nonsensical way that we started looking up what the "source" language might have been (it's Russian) [*] Some references (like команда хрустяшек > team crunchy) are lost in translation. Not much that you can do about this, just be aware that it made sense in Russian. [/list] Bugs: [list] [*] Can't pick up cooked food from the ground sometimes as a client (host still can) [*] Raccoons periodically bug out and don't do anything https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3732143905 [*] Visitors can clip through geometry if they feel like it https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3732198110 [*] Coins left by visitors don't always disappear client-side [*] Garbage ("goop") can cause dirty dishes and/or orders to clip through tables because they have physics enabled and it doesn't. [/list]

总结省流：游戏不错，但是有赌博。 我详细说原因，游戏上，胡闹厨房的基本盘还有诸多点子非常有趣，就是天赋做得有点差，非常值得小伙伴一起玩耍，我重点说差评的赌博。这游戏单独的胡闹厨房打工没问题，赌博单独拿出来做游戏没问题，但是结合在一起就有问题了，会让你强烈感受到，什么叫做打工不如赌博，崩坏玩家的打工价值观，从而发展到现实自己身上：是不是自己也拿现金去赌场搏一搏？某种意义上讲，这种结合也是很成功的，但是对社会主义价值观有冲突，我也很理智的知道自己有点神经质，如同看动画片就担心小朋友学坏然后举报动画片一样，但是我觉得需要有我这样的声音。也许有人会说，我不碰赌博这块不就行了？兄弟你忍不住，这游戏迟早有一天你会崩盘，最后剩下来几十块钱，你脑子一激灵不如梭哈一手，赌输了就算了，最怕是赌赢了，然后停不下来赢到上万，你会发现打工一天累死累活，利润不够赌场放一手牌。西大因为这个挂掉的人还少吗。 PS：如果单纯玩游戏，我觉得价格稍微贵一点点，打折可入

So. This might look like a cute lil rat game, like a cute lil lets-cook-and-greet-customers-game but hear me out. Dont be fooled by the cute little rat noses, funny outfits or smooth designs. This is war. You need to get faster. You need to get more efficient. You need to learn to optimize your processes. You need to look better. You need to gamble harder. You need to be nicer to the guests. You need to know what they want; YOU NEED TO BE IT ALL. So i started playing this game with friends and eventually started a solo ratstaurante. Im not gonna lie, im a little annoyed I have to constantly cook fish, meat, eggs etc. as i personally dont consume meat. But i really enjoy this game in general. I am at a point, where i need to decide how desperately i want a fridge. And my god. I really want a fridge. But i also need space for the bazillions of dishes i have to cook/combine in no time as soon as guests arrive. So here i am with the big life choices. Whats it gonna be? I think you should buy and play the game and decide for yourself - it's so worth it.
